title: Advanced Browser Artifacts & Reconstruction 🧩
description: Recover cached pages, analyze extensions, session data, and even incognito traces.

slides.title: Cache: The Snapshot Archive 🖼️
slides.content:
# What the Browser Keeps for Performance

The cache stores local copies of web resources (images, scripts, CSS, even whole pages) to speed up loading. For forensics, it’s a snapshot of what the user saw.

- **Chrome**: `Cache/` folder with `data_0`, `data_1`, `f_xxxxxx` files and an `index` file. Tools like **ChromeCacheView** can parse it.
- **Firefox**: `cache2/` directory with entries and a `cache2.sqlite` indexing database.
- **Edge**: Similar to Chrome.

Cache can show:
- Images from a website (even if deleted later)
- Downloaded script files (malware)
- Timestamps of when cached (often matching visit times)

Deleted cache entries may be recovered via file carving on the disk image.

quizData.question: What is the forensic value of browser cache?

options.text: It contains the user's passwords in plaintext
It provides copies of web content the user accessed
It records IP addresses of visited sites

quizData.explanation: Cache holds actual files like images and HTML, proving what the user saw.

slides.title: Session Recovery & Open Tabs 🔄
slides.content:
Browsers often save the state of open tabs to restore after a crash or update.

- **Chrome**: `Current Tabs`, `Current Session`, `Tabs_*` files in `Sessions` folder. They are in SNSS format (binary). Tools like **SessionExtractor** parse them.
- **Firefox**: `sessionstore.jsonlz4` (compressed JSON) in the profile. It contains current open tabs, closed tabs (recent), and even tab history.
- **Edge**: Same as Chrome.

This can reveal what the user was viewing right before they closed the browser – including incognito windows if they crashed and were restored.

slides.title: Extract Firefox Session Tabs
slides.codeSnippet:
python3 lz4json.py sessionstore.jsonlz4 > session.json
# Then grep for "url": to list all open and recently closed tabs.

quizData.question: Incognito/Private browsing mode never leaves any trace on disk.
quizData.explanation: Incognito avoids writing to main history/cookies, but crash recovery files, DNS cache, or memory dumps may still contain traces.

slides.title: Extensions & Plugins 🧩
slides.content:
Browser extensions can store data locally. For example, a crypto wallet extension might store transaction history. Extensions live in:
- Chrome: `Extensions/<id>/` with `local storage` (levelDB) and `IndexedDB`.
- Firefox: `extensions/<id>.xpi` and storage in profile.

Check for:
- Ad blockers (could indicate privacy‑conscious user)
- VPN extensions (used to bypass restrictions)
- Password manager extensions (may store master‑password hints)

Analyzing extension data can be crucial for understanding user intent.

quizData.question: Which browser storage type is commonly used by extensions to save data locally?
quizData.explanation: Extensions use Web Storage APIs (localStorage, IndexedDB) or LevelDB to store data.

slides.title: DNS & Network Artifacts 🌐
slides.content:
Even with private browsing, the OS’s **DNS cache** records domain lookups. On Windows, `ipconfig /displaydns` shows cached DNS entries. On Linux, `systemd-resolve --statistics` or `/var/cache/nscd/hosts`.

Also, the **hosts file** may show blocked sites. Proxy settings and VPN logs (if any) can reveal traffic.

Router netflow or firewall logs also capture DNS queries – a powerful supplement.

slides.title: Reconstructing the User’s Web Journey 🧭
slides.content:
## Piecing Together the Timeline

Combine:
- Browser **history** (URL, timestamp)
- **Cookies** (first‑party and third‑party)
- **Cache** (actual content)
- **Downloads** (files saved)
- **Bookmarks** (intentional saves)
- **Search terms** (from `History` `keyword_search_terms` table)

Example: A user searched for “bomb making”, visited a site, cached the page, downloaded a PDF, and bookmarked another page. This sequence proves intent and knowledge.

Tools like **BrowsingHistoryView** or **Hindsight** can aggregate all these artifacts into a single report.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use Hindsight for Chrome

Hindsight is an open‑source tool that parses Chrome’s history, cookies, cache, downloads, and more into a single timeline. It can also decrypt cookies if you provide the DPAPI master key.
